text.title: Process Mining and Intelligent Automation Analysis Core Rules
text.summary: Testable rules grounding the process-mining-automation methodology. Each rule pairs a binary check + sourced rationale and is referenced from `content/06-decision-tree.xml`. Process mining definition, BA competencies required, four-step workflow, and tool landscape. Six-criterion scoring matrix for automation readiness, RPA vs. intelligent automation comparison, and key vendor landscape.

section.title: Background

list.item: Technical: ProM, Disco, or Celonis (process mining tools), SQL for event log extraction, data visualization for conformance reports
Process: BPMN 2.0 notation, process modeling, workflow variance analysis
Analytical: statistics (frequency distributions, variant analysis), pattern recognition, root-cause analysis of process deviations
Domain: industry-specific knowledge to interpret discovered process variants and regulatory understanding for compliance-sensitive processes
Celonis: process mining market leader, enterprise SaaS, strong action orientation and EMS (execution management system) integration
Disco (Fluxicon): desktop tool, fast for initial exploration, imports XES and CSV event logs
ProM: open-source research platform, most algorithms, requires technical expertise
Microsoft Power Automate Process Advisor: M365-integrated process mining for organizations already in the Microsoft ecosystem
RPA: rule-based repetitive tasks, predefined decision logic, structured data only, no learning, human escalation for exceptions — best for high-volume stable processes

Intelligent Automation: complex variable tasks, AI-driven decisions, structured and unstructured data, continuous learning, autonomous exception handling — best for variable processes with document complexity or judgment requirements
UiPath: largest pure-play RPA, enterprise leader, strong developer ecosystem and test automation integration
Automation Anywhere: cloud-native architecture, strong AI integration, IQ Bot for document processing
Blue Prism: enterprise governance and auditability focus, preferred in regulated industries
Microsoft Power Automate: M365 integration, low barrier for Microsoft shops, desktop and cloud flows
Celonis: process mining combined with automation recommendations, action engine triggers RPA from discovered bottlenecks

section.p: Market context: RPA market: $35.27 billion in 2026 growing to $247.34 billion by 2035. 58% of enterprises will use RPA with AI/ML by 2026. 44% already use AI-enabled RPA for document processing. By 2026, 30% of enterprises will automate more than 50% of network activities.

rule.statement: Step 1 (profile logs): Schema completeness + case-id quality check; reject if below threshold.
rule.rationale: Skipping or reordering this step breaks the methodology's invariants; it is the profile logs gate.

rule.statement: Step 2 (discover): Run miner; emit as-is BPMN.
rule.rationale: Skipping or reordering this step breaks the methodology's invariants; it is the discover gate.

rule.statement: Step 3 (conformance check): Token replay; identify deviations + fitness score.
rule.rationale: Skipping or reordering this step breaks the methodology's invariants; it is the conformance check gate.

rule.statement: Step 4 (score candidates): Apply matrix; total score with breakdown.
rule.rationale: Skipping or reordering this step breaks the methodology's invariants; it is the score candidates gate.

rule.statement: Step 5 (assess verdict and roi): Pick verdict per candidate; estimate ROI.
rule.rationale: Skipping or reordering this step breaks the methodology's invariants; it is the assess verdict and roi gate.

rule.statement: Apply process mining to reconstruct actual process flows from IT system event logs before documenting process requirements or selecting automation candidates. Do not rely on stakeholder interviews alone for process discovery — actual execution diverges from documented processes in the majority of cases.
rule.rationale: Stakeholder interviews capture the ideal process; event logs capture what actually happens. RPA initiatives built on interview-based process models fail because they automate the documented process, not the real one.

rule.statement: Process mining follows four steps in sequence: (1) Event Log Extraction — extract case ID, activity, timestamp from IT systems; (2) Process Discovery — generate actual process model from event log; (3) Conformance Checking — compare discovered model to documented design, identify deviations and their frequency; (4) Enhancement — use deviation analysis to identify bottlenecks, rework loops, and automation candidates.
rule.rationale: Skipping conformance checking (step 3) produces a "what is" model without identifying where and how often the process deviates from intent — the most actionable output for process improvement.

rule.statement: Score every automation candidate against six criteria: Volume (high = more than 100 transactions/day), Standardization (high = rule-based with few exceptions), Stability (medium = process unchanged more than 6 months), Digital Input (medium = structured data available), Error Rate (medium = high manual error frequency), ROI Potential (high = high labor cost with measurable payback). Total out of 30. Recommend: full automation above 24, partial automation 18-24, process improvement first 12-18, not suitable below 12.
rule.rationale: Without a scoring matrix, automation selection is based on who has the loudest stakeholder voice. The matrix forces objective measurement across dimensions that predict automation success.

rule.statement: Choose the automation class from the process characteristics, not from the vendor: rule-based, structured-input, stable processes get RPA; variable processes with unstructured documents or judgment steps get intelligent automation. Complete the six-criterion matrix before any vendor conversation.
rule.rationale: RPA has no learning and escalates every exception to a human, so it breaks on variance; intelligent automation handles unstructured data and exceptions autonomously but costs more. Vendor-first selection locks in the architecture before the process characteristics are known.

rule.statement: If preconditions for process-mining-automation do not hold, do not apply this methodology; route to an alternative as the decision tree suggests.
rule.rationale: Methodologies misapplied to wrong contexts create overhead without value; explicit skip preserves the agent's budget.
